retro.headline: Sewer commission approved the Q2 FY27 commitment and aimed to hold a January 12 hearing on late fees.
retro.summary: The commission heard about an irrigation deduct meter billing error caused by wrong reading dates from the water department and a billing system rate setting, since corrected. It was told the CTE contract bid was postponed and the current contract extended three months, reviewed Fitchburg and Leominster flow capacity, and discussed the sewer demand fee and interest rate. It voted the quarterly commitment and agreed to take up the budget line by line, including preventive maintenance, on December 8.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted, 3 in favor on a roll call, to approve the Q2 fiscal year 27 sewer commitment.
The commission plans a public hearing on sewer rates and the demand fee for January 12, with firm numbers to be set at the next meeting.
Staff compared late fees and interest in surrounding towns; the commission leans toward a modest increase below the state maximum.
The commission heard that wrong reading dates from the water department gave some customers too large an irrigation meter deduct in Q1; bills were corrected and remailed.
The CTE contract was extended three months at the existing rate while the bid is re-posted.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills may rise through a higher demand fee or late-interest rate, and residents can speak at the planned January hearing before those rates are set.
Residents with irrigation deduct meters should check that their corrected Q1 and Q2 bills match their meter readings.
The budget, including whether money is set aside for preventive maintenance after an emergency pump replacement, is still open and will shape future sewer costs.
watch_next: December 8 meeting: line-by-line budget discussion, including preventive maintenance.
January 12: planned public hearing on sewer rates and the demand fee, with firm numbers to be set at the next meeting.

retro.headline: Board referred Pratt Street speeding to police; food pantry suspends operations; flag policy leans restrictive.
retro.summary: Pratt Street residents asked for help with speeding and the board referred it to the police chief and DPW. The food pantry said it is suspending regular operations because it cannot move out of TC Passios by December 1; the board informally supported a DPW bay for pop-ups and set an executive session on the license agreement. The board also prepared for Special Town Meeting, worked through handbook chapters 7 to 12, leaned toward a restrictive flag policy, and approved an appointment, a fee waiver and minutes.

what_happened.line: The food pantry said it is suspending regular operations because it cannot move out of TC Passios by December 1; the board informally backed a DPW bay for pop-ups.
The board set an executive session on the 24th for the food pantry license agreement and asked for a liability letter for cold storage.
Pratt Street speeding was referred to the police chief and DPW, to return on a future agenda after residents described fast traffic and no sidewalks.
The board reached consensus on the more restrictive flag policy, to add half-staff language and send it to town counsel.
Article 9 stays deferred until the school committee acts, and the board ratified an appointment, an ADA committee seat and a fee waiver unanimously.

why_it_matters: Residents who use the food pantry may find regular distribution unavailable until a new site is settled, and the town has not yet committed to one.
Pratt Street speed measures such as a lower limit or speed bumps depend on a later board agenda and on police and DPW review.
Free cash will not be certified by the special town meeting, which limits what that meeting can draw on.
watch_next: Executive session on the 24th on the food pantry license agreement.
Return of the Pratt Street speeding referral on a future board agenda.

retro.headline: Council on Aging backed a push for a shower and official shelter at the center, and sent a member to the School Committee on elevator signs.
retro.summary: The council took up small ADA fixes around town, a possible building expansion with a shower so the center could serve as an emergency shelter, and the holiday party. It heard the parking lot design update and a policies-and-procedures task force report. A resident criticised a member's remarks at the last meeting, and the director's report was read in her absence.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging voted to have a member take steps toward adding a shower and making the center an official emergency shelter, including a capital plan request.
The council voted to send a member to the School Committee on its behalf about elevator signage and other ADA items.
A member volunteered for the town ADA committee, and the council discussed small ADA fixes at town hall described as modest expenses.
The council heard that the parking lot design contract has been issued, with pricing to follow and a separate capital request expected.
The council set a December meeting of the policies task force, with policy suggestions due by the end of November and a vote at a later meeting.

why_it_matters: A shower and shelter designation would turn the senior center into an emergency shelter, and the expansion and the parking lot would need capital funding that residents may be asked to approve at Town Meeting or through the capital plan.
Council priorities for the FY28 budget, such as meals site staffing and homebound services, feed into the town budget, which is mostly taxes.
watch_next: Pricing for the parking lot work, then a standalone capital request for town meeting or the next capital plan cycle.
Telehealth hub ribbon cutting on January 12, 2027, after the board meeting; policy suggestions due by end of November.

retro.headline: Committee declined to weigh in on the track article, kept the senior center network project, and set meetings for Nov 19 and Nov 30.
retro.summary: The Capital Planning Committee reviewed its charter duties, then discussed whether to weigh in on the school's Article 9 track and field engineering request for the Nov 17 special town meeting. It concluded it would not make a recommendation because the item had not gone through its process, though capital projects should come through it. It then voted on keeping the Adult Activity Center network upgrade in the FY27 plan after its quote fell below the capital threshold, and scheduled department presentations.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee voted 4-1 to keep the Adult Activity Center network upgrade in the FY27 capital program and told IT to give far more accurate quotes in future.
The committee will make no recommendation on the school's Article 9 track and field engineering request, saying it did not go through the committee's process.
The committee advised that all capital projects should come through it.
The network upgrade had been planned just over the capital threshold and came in under it after a vendor quote.
A tentative Nov 19 meeting was set for police and fire, with Nov 30 and Dec 7 at 6:30 for DPW, school and facilities.

why_it_matters: Article 9 goes to the Nov 17 special town meeting without a recommendation from the committee that reviews capital projects, so voters will decide it without that review.
The upcoming department presentations are where requests for the FY27 capital plan, which draws on the town budget, mostly taxes, will be heard.
watch_next: Nov 17 special town meeting vote on Article 9, the track and field engineering and design study.
Capital Planning meetings tentatively on Nov 19 (police and fire), then Nov 30 and Dec 7 at 6:30 (DPW, school, facilities).

retro.headline: Cable committee heard a space-planning pitch for its studio and saw a first FY28 draft budget showing a deficit; reorganization tabled.
retro.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee vice chair discussed using town hall's second floor or other space for the PAC studio and office, and the committee gave feedback on needs. The manager reviewed her activities and a preliminary FY28 budget, which is a draft to be reviewed with the town manager. Reorganization was tabled, prior minutes were approved, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The committee saw a first draft FY28 budget that shows a deficit, because draft revenue is lower than last year while expenses are slightly under.
The manager said the draft is unconfirmed with the town accountant and will be reviewed with the town manager before it comes back for approval.
The Municipal Building Design Committee vice chair discussed using town hall's second floor or other space for the PAC studio and office, and the committee gave feedback.
Reorganization of chair and vice chair was tabled, and the vice chair stays acting chair for now.
Policy review will start in January, two policies at a time; a meeting with the attorney on studio space is set for November 23.

why_it_matters: Cable access is funded largely by Comcast payments, which are declining, so a recurring deficit puts pressure on PAC's reserves and on local meeting coverage.
Where the studio lands in the town's space plan, and what the 2028 Comcast renewal does to funding, will decide what the town spends to keep public access running.
watch_next: Meeting with the attorney on studio space, Monday, November 23.
Next PAC meeting, December 7, and the FY28 budget coming back after review with the town manager.

retro.headline: Planning Board endorsed five ANR plans and approved a shared-driveway special permit at 760 Goodrich Street.
retro.summary: The board endorsed ANR plans for five properties, then held a hearing on a shared driveway at 760 Goodrich Street. It approved the special permit with a homeowners association condition and accepted a de minimis stormwater change. It also extended a stormwater bond for 100 Townsend Harbor Road, heard committee reports and approved minutes.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved a special permit for a shared driveway at 760 Goodrich Street, with a homeowners association condition before occupancy permits.
The board found a stormwater alteration at 760 Goodrich de minimis and accepted the change.
The board endorsed ANR plans for five properties, including Howard Street, Leominster Road, Sunny Hill Road, Mass Ave and Northfield Road.
The board extended the stormwater bond for 100 Townsend Harbor Road through July 1, 2028, after the builder asked for more time.
The director will write the 760 Goodrich decision for members, with signing to follow if no changes come by next Monday.

why_it_matters: The Goodrich Street permit sets a homeowners association condition on a shared driveway, which decides who is responsible for it once homes are occupied.
The bond extension at Townsend Harbor Road keeps stormwater security in place for five lots while construction runs longer, which protects the town from paying for unfinished drainage work.
watch_next: Signing of the 760 Goodrich Street decision, expected after next Monday if members request no changes.
Next Planning Board meetings on November 23, December 14 and January 11 and 25; none on December 28.

retro.headline: Stormwater task force reviewed the ERU fee spreadsheet, fixed outliers, and prepared slides for Monday's library session.
retro.summary: The task force went through the scrubbed ERU/utility fee spreadsheet, correcting blank use codes, a large quarry property, the Carousel Lane and Tri Town entries, and renaming a column to impervious area. They agreed the figures are a best-effort starting point open to review, planned to send the file to FinCom via a town contact but not post it online, and arranged a Friday Zoom to review slides before a Monday public session at the library. A roll call vote was taken to adjourn.

what_happened.line: The task force worked through the scrubbed utility fee spreadsheet and corrected blank use codes, the large quarry property, and the Carousel Lane and Tri Town entries.
The column header was changed to impervious area, with a note that the spreadsheet figures are best effort and open to review.
The spreadsheet will not be posted online; it will go to a town contact to share with FinCom.
The task force said the fee is expected near the stated level but is not final, and new permit requirements could raise costs.
A Zoom review of the slides was set for Friday at 9:00, ahead of a Monday public session at the library.

why_it_matters: The stormwater utility fee would be a new charge on property owners, and the figures behind it are still a draft that could change before any bill is set.
Unpaid fees would go on tax liens, so a missed payment could carry a delay of over a year and possible legal fees.
watch_next: Friday 9:00 Zoom review of the slides among three members.
Monday public session at the library, which is to be posted as a meeting.

retro.headline: Committee renewed MASC membership 3-2 and passed over the special education reserve fund article at Town Meeting.
retro.summary: The committee approved backlog minutes, accepted PTO donations, held an anti-bullying plan hearing, and heard a long superintendent report on public records requests and central office staff. It voted to renew MASC membership over strong objection, and to pass over the special education reserve fund article until a finance director can help write a policy. It also discussed FY28 budget priorities, with no decisions and no numbers.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 3-2 to renew its MASC membership and pay the bill, after debate over whether the dues are worth the cost.
The committee voted to pass over the special education reserve fund article at Town Meeting; the chair will tell the select board a policy will wait for a new finance director.
The committee accepted PTO donations to Turkey Hill, the Middle School, the High School and the Primary School, all by unanimous votes.
The superintendent said the district will begin charging for public records requests that need significant staff time.
FY28 budget priorities were discussed without decisions; the town manager is to give the budget number at the end of November and school budgets are due December 18.

why_it_matters: Passing over the special education reserve article means no reserve policy will be before Town Meeting this cycle, so how the district sets money aside for unexpected special education costs stays unsettled until a policy is written.

Public records fees and the FY28 budget limits set by the town manager's number both bear on what residents pay and how much the schools can spend, which feeds into the budget that voters and taxpayers will be asked to consider.
watch_next: The anti-bullying plan revisions return for a vote at the next School Committee meeting.
The town manager's budget number is due at the end of November; school budgets are due December 18.

retro.headline: Commission approved the Island Road septic and Sunset Lane retaining walls; a sand-area request was withdrawn.
retro.summary: The commission heard several wetlands filings: a dock extension, a sandy-area request on Spring Street Extension that was withdrawn without prejudice, a septic replacement and a retaining wall replacement, and some continuances. It also issued two certificates of compliance. Other business covered tree clearing on Reservoir Road, unsafe trail footbridges, Hollis Road house renovation and custodian plans, and the stormwater utility.

what_happened.line: The commission approved a septic system replacement at 143 Island Road as submitted, 5-0.
It approved a retaining wall replacement at 386 Sunset Lane as submitted, 4-0, with one member recused.
The applicant for a sandy-area request on Spring Street Extension withdrew it without prejudice; no vote was taken.
A dock extension at 25 Cliff View Terrace received a negative determination, 5-0, and two certificates of compliance for Cushing Lane were approved, 5-0.

retro.headline: Stormwater task force found errors in its draft fee spreadsheet and agreed to fix it and meet again Wednesday.
retro.summary: The task force debriefed on its Select Board and Finance Committee presentations, then reviewed a member's spreadsheet of stormwater fees against current tax bills. Members found the fee column did not match the stated per-unit rate, agreed to drop the 10% cap column, simplify the sheet, and handle multi-unit properties as exceptions. They planned the public info session and town meeting presentations, and approved prior minutes and adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force found that the fee column in its draft spreadsheet did not match the stated per-unit rate, and agreed to correct it.
Members agreed to drop the 10% cap column and not apply a cap.
Multi-unit properties such as Carousel Lane will go on a separate exceptions tab, and the columns will be renamed with a use-code key and ERU explanation.
The task force will meet by Zoom Wednesday at 6 pm to sign off on the corrected spreadsheet once it is circulated.
Presenters were chosen for the public info session and town meeting, and a formal task force vote on the warrant article goes on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: The spreadsheet compares a proposed stormwater fee with each property's current tax bill, so errors in it would change what owners are told they would pay.
If stormwater were funded through the operating budget instead of a separate utility fee, the budget line would have to rise and tax bills would go up.
watch_next: Zoom meeting Wednesday at 6 pm to sign off on the corrected spreadsheet, after it is circulated.
A formal task force vote on the warrant article, set for the next agenda, and the posted public info session.

retro.headline: Sewer Commission voted to send a delinquent Sunny Hill Road account to the tax collector with no payment plan.
retro.summary: The commission voted to refer a long-delinquent sewer account to the tax collector for tax lien and decline a payment plan. It also heard updates on a contract RFR and second-quarter billing, and began discussing raising the sewer demand fee and interest rate, held for a later meeting with a public hearing required. It voted to move the December 29 meeting to January 12.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to send the balance on a delinquent Sunny Hill Road account to the tax collector for a tax lien and not to offer a payment plan.
The DPW director's suggested monthly payment plan, covering most of a year's bill with any remainder going on the tax lien, was rejected.
The commission began discussing a higher sewer demand fee and interest rate; counsel said the legal maximum rate is above the current one. It was held for a later meeting.
A request for responses for contractor services went out, with bids due in mid-November, to place a contractor before the current contract expires.
The commission voted to move the December 29 Zoom meeting to January 12.

why_it_matters: Sewer fees are billed to property owners, and an account left unpaid can be added to the property's tax bill as a lien, so this vote shows how the town collects overdue sewer charges.
Any change to the demand fee or interest rate would change what sewer users are billed, and the commission said it needs a public hearing with newspaper notice first.
watch_next: Demand fee and interest rate discussion returns at a meeting when Chip is present, after the business manager gathers comparable towns' fees; a public hearing is required to change the regulation.
Next meetings: Nov 10 (hybrid at DPW), Nov 24 (Zoom), Dec 8 (hybrid), then Jan 12, 2027.

retro.headline: Select Board recommended disapproval of the special ed reserve transfer and deferred budget and track articles for the Nov 17 special town meeting.
retro.summary: The board reviewed the draft special town meeting warrant, voting on recommendations for several articles and deferring others pending certified free cash. It also discussed a draft flag policy, whether to draft a special education reserve fund policy (referred back to the school committee), and heard the town manager's report including a delay in free cash certification.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-1 to recommend disapproval of Article 4, a transfer from free cash to the special education reserve fund.
The board deferred Articles 2 and 3, and separately Article 9 (track and field engineering), to be voted on after the town knows its certified free cash.
The board recommended approval of Articles 1, 5 and 6, took no position 4-1 on the non-binding straw polls in Articles 7 and 8, and approved the warrant.
A motion to have the town manager draft a special education reserve fund policy was withdrawn; the matter goes to the school committee chair for their agenda first.
The town manager reported that year-end close is slow and free cash may not be certified in time for the special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Several warrant articles depend on free cash, and until it is certified the board cannot finalize recommendations on them, so voters at the special town meeting may be asked to act on items the board has not yet weighed in on.

Article 4 would move money from free cash into a special education reserve, a fund that cushions the town budget, which is mostly taxes, against unplanned placement costs, and the board's recommendation against it is advisory only; Town Meeting makes the decision.
watch_next: Nov 17: the board meets at 6:30, before the special town meeting, to vote on the deferred articles, then Town Meeting votes on the warrant.
Nov 10: Select Board meeting, partly a workshop on the draft flag policy.
